cells.tense: Right here the whole of the thing is in view and you are the one choosing which way it points.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Choose something you already understand. Follow how it works, step by step, to its logical end, until the conclusion sits plain. Then stop.
cells.core:
Here the whole of something is in view — the parts, the shape of it, the way it has been going — and none of that is the difficulty. What is asked of you is the next move: not every true thing needs to be the thing you keep. You are the one pointing it.

Try this. Choose something you already understand and follow how it works all the way to its logical end, one step at a time, until the conclusion sits plain. Do it for the doing, not to prove anything. When the reasoning lands, the picture settles and what you hold is a choice you actually made.
cells.sheetLine: You see it whole. Step it to the end, then move.
cells.verb: seeing the whole of a thing and holding to the direction it asks for
cells.place: in the moment where you choose what gets your attention next

cells.tense: Before the thing has even happened, the whole reading of it is already finished and the move is made.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Whatever starts soon, however small, hold the first flicker of it a day with nothing aimed at it. No plan. Watch what it wants to be.
cells.core:
You read things fast and completely, so the answer tends to arrive before the event does. Nothing is hidden; the shape is already in your hands, and the hands have already moved. What gets clipped is the stretch where the thing is still just beginning and nobody, including you, has fixed what it means.

Let one beginning stay a beginning. Whatever starts soon — a decision, a shift, something half-said — hold off steering it through a day. Freshness can itch when you are used to sorting at once. What the day buys is a move that comes after the thing, not ahead of it.

cells.tense: What was understood has been sitting finished for some time, and still nobody built a form from it.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Take something you already understand deeply. Write a single line naming what it is for and what shape it would take. One line, nothing beneath it.
cells.core:
When this works, understanding turns into a form you can point at — the whole of something held, then one clear thing made from it. At the moment the understanding is complete and the form is missing; comprehension is not short, the whole of it is held and held well, but nothing was picked up and built with, so it sits finished and unspent.

Give it one seed. Take something you already understand deeply and write a single line naming what it is for and what shape it would take. No branch under the line. That line is not the building; it is the first held piece, small enough for one hand. From that much, direction can start without anyone pushing.

cells.tense: The direction is being set in this very moment and nobody is claiming the setting as theirs.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: When the next thing comes in — a message, a change, a suggestion — take it as it arrives, one beat, before you decide what it is for.
cells.core:
You are setting direction right now — attention here, not there — and it does not register as a choice. It registers as the situation requiring it, or the context making it obvious. That is how steering feels from inside when nobody signed for it. The steering happens anyway, and it works.

Let one arrival stay new. When the next thing comes in — a message, a change, a suggestion — take it as it arrives for one beat before you decide what it is for. The newness is real even when your certainty is fast. Catching yourself mid-set is what makes the direction yours to make, instead of yours to find already made.
